question: Should OpenClaw add a new per-agent `subagents.workspace` config surface for same-agent default sub-agents, or keep workspace isolation routed through explicit target agents plus `requireAgentId` and sandbox policy?
rationale: The source confirms the requested config is missing and same-agent children inherit the requester workspace, but adding a new workspace selector changes a security-sensitive public config boundary rather than fixing a documented bug.

options.title: Prefer explicit target agents
options.body: Keep the current model where isolated child workspaces require a configured target agent and optionally `requireAgentId`, then improve docs or diagnostics if maintainers want the path clearer.

options.title: Approve narrow workspace override
options.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.workspace` only with explicit schema, docs, same-agent and cross-agent tests, and sandbox/Codex bootstrap contract coverage.

options.title: Fold into broader isolation design
options.body: Defer this issue behind the broader skill/workdir isolation discussion if maintainers want one coherent workspace-isolation API instead of multiple knobs.

recommendation.title: Prefer explicit target agents
recommendation.body: Keep the current model where isolated child workspaces require a configured target agent and optionally `requireAgentId`, then improve docs or diagnostics if maintainers want the path clearer.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses config policy, security posture, and current docs/vision framing, where recent history points to steipete as the best available routing candidate.
